           # SV-EXH-PROOF.5.2.4.1 — use the typedef-EXCLUDING sibling here, not the
           # permissive `provisional_unscoped_block_class_type`. The provisional rule
           # is gated only by `has_fact(type_name, head)`, so a plain `typedef int T`
           # head passed even with a `::P` scope_chain — making `localparam int Y = T::P`
           # wrongly parseable (T::P is invalid per IEEE 1800 when T is not a class/
           # package; sv_semantic_scope_contract case `parameter_typedef_fail`).
           # `known_unscoped_block_class_type` adds the correct
           # `lacks_fact_attribute_equals(type_name, head, declaration_family, typedef)`
           # gate (same `{head, params, scope_chain}` shape, so the emitted
           # `provisional_class_type` AST kind is unchanged). Bare typedef-as-datatype
           # `T x;` is unaffected (it matches `known_unscoped_data_type_identifier`
           # above). `block_data_type` keeps the permissive `provisional_*` branch for
